=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:lines 236-288 (_mt_gate) | severity=blocker | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The code recomputes blockers from the live open-PR list on every gate run and re-adds `ai:merge-queued` whenever blockers are non-empty, with no check for whether an operator intentionally removed the label.
  WHY: An operator who reads the comment, removes `ai:merge-queued`, and re-runs review sees the gate immediately re-add the label and re-queue the PR — the documented escape hatch does not exist.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:lines 83-88 (case statement on MT_ENABLED) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The enabled-flag parser accepts only six spellings: `true`, `TRUE`, `True`, `1`, `yes`, `on`.
  WHY: Values such as `YES`, `ON`, `Yes`, `On`, `tRue`, and `TruE` disable the train despite the case-insensitive documentation.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:lines 816-825, `seen_pairs: set[tuple[str, str]]` | severity=nit | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `seen_pairs` deduplication set is dead code.
  WHY: The nested loop visits each unordered pair exactly once, and the set is never read by the non-empty-scope branch.
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh:_mt_dispatch_review (lines 294-302), called from _mt_release (lines 304-345) | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The release dispatch issues `gh workflow run` without checking whether a review run is already in-flight for the same PR.
  WHY: Concurrent release invocations can dispatch duplicate reviews, causing an extra reviewer/editor cycle.
- .github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml:line 215, `if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true` | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The merge-train release step only fires when the closed blocker PR was merged.
  WHY: A queued PR in a core-profile repo whose sole blocker is closed unmerged stays queued forever because no other release trigger may run.
